reference_case_concept_lines: ECHA EUSES water screening case family: This governed reference case family anchors one-compartment flowing-water screening interpretations against regulator-recognizable EUSES-style environmental exposure concepts.

EPA flow-through water screening case family: This governed reference case family anchors finite-duration flowing-water screening logic against EPA environmental model guidance for bounded transport and model-use transparency.

Advective clearance edge-condition case family: This governed reference case family anchors the experimental advective screening model at the two reviewer-critical clearance extremes: short residence time and long residence time under effective persistence.

ECHA bounded-clearance edge case family: This governed reference case family anchors screening claims about bounded concentration under effective persistence when a finite residence-time loss term remains present.
EPA elapsed-time environmental model case family: This governed reference case family anchors elapsed-time and post-release-decay reasoning against EPA environmental model evaluation principles.

EPA post-release decay bucket case family: This governed reference case family anchors post-release elapsed-time decay behavior in bucketed screening outputs against EPA environmental model evaluation principles.

ECHA elapsed-time flowing-water screening case family: This governed reference case family anchors elapsed-time bucket behavior for one-compartment flowing-water screening to regulator-recognizable EU environmental assessment concepts.

Advective duration plateau case family: This governed reference case family anchors long-duration finite screening behavior where the combined degradation-plus-clearance term drives the solution toward a duration-limited plateau.

ECHA transition-boundary screening case family: This governed reference case family anchors near-parity flowing-water screening interpretations against regulator-recognizable EU environmental assessment concepts where residence time and degradation compete within the same bounded loss term.

EPA transition-boundary screening case family: This governed reference case family anchors reviewer-facing interpretation of near-parity loss regimes where modest parameter changes can flip the dominant screening loss term.

EPA turnover-boundary screening case family: This governed reference case family anchors reviewer-facing interpretation of residence-time turnover windows where a one-compartment flowing-water screen moves between storage-dominant, intermediate, and flow-through transport behavior.

OECD bounded-transport screening case family: This governed reference case family anchors finite, bounded one-compartment transport reasoning where retained mass approaches a loss-limited plateau rather than growing without bound.

EPA post-release flushing screening case family: This governed reference case family anchors post-release flushing and retained-mass decline against EPA environmental model evaluation principles for time-varying screening scenarios.

OECD post-release recovery screening case family: This governed reference case family anchors post-release recovery interpretation against OECD degradation-and-accumulation reporting concepts for deterministic screening models.

ECHA post-release flushing boundary case family: This governed reference case family anchors reviewer-facing interpretation of post-release recovery windows that sit near the one-turnover flushing boundary in a flowing-water screening model.

EPA post-release recovery directionality case family: This governed reference case family anchors reviewer-facing interpretation of how retained release-stop mass should progress as the post-release recovery window moves from below the one-turnover flushing boundary to beyond it.

EPA post-release combined-loss recovery pace case family: This governed reference case family anchors reviewer-facing interpretation of how quickly retained release-stop mass should halve under the combined degradation-plus-clearance loss constant in a flowing-water screening model.

OECD post-release half-recovery directionality case family: This governed reference case family anchors reviewer-facing interpretation of how retained release-stop mass should progress from above the 50% combined-loss recovery anchor to materially below it as the post-release window extends under the same resolved loss constants.
